evidence.note: Upfront decomposition into 6 tasks ordered by dependency (schema/store → http_app → broadcast → IRC → SPA → supervisor), building foundations before dependents rather than working wherever attention lands.

Broadcast relay designed with a DB-polling fallback 'so fan-out survives' when relay is dead — proactively front-loading the high-risk broadcast-kill/dense-seq resilience invariant before it was tested, showing awareness that it gates many checks.
Verification deliberately targets the load-bearing invariants: relay-kill, node kill, replay/resume across nodes, dense seq with relay dead — the highest-coverage/highest-risk systems.
Explicit check that required SPA testids (static and dynamic) are present — another gating invariant for the browser grader, indicating conscious coverage of pinned hooks.

Broad coverage of the full feature surface (files, search, invitations, mentions, groups, slash commands, DMs, roles, permissions) all built and tested fully — no visible intentional deferral or minimal-viable trade-down of lower-yield features.

reasoning: The agent front-loaded foundations and, notably, designed the resilience fallback into the broadcast layer proactively (step 18), then verified the gating invariants — seq density, node/relay kill, testids — which is meaningfully above the level-5 'roughly targets big-ticket first' anchor. However, there is no observed explicit value/coverage weighting prose, and no conscious 'minimal viable' or deferral decisions (the entire feature surface was built out), so it falls short of the level-8 anchor's deliberate risk-weighted allocation and budget reallocation. This lands at 6, interpolating between the 5 and 8 anchors.
